newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico budget surplus at 19.644 bln pesos in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Mexico budget surplus at 19.644 bln pesos in Q3.

text.p: Mexico racked up a public sector surplus of 19.644 billion pesos at the end of the third quarter, the Finance Ministry said Saturday.

It said there was a higher-than-expected surplus due to the lower cost of public debt payments, the cutting back of non-priority current spending and higher oil prices on the international markets fetched by state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos.

Mexico's primary public surplus, excluding items such as interest payments on debt, was 85.392 billion pesos at the end of the third quarter, compared to a primary surplus of 76.394 billion during the same period a year earlier.

It said budget income was 396.26 billion pesos during the year's first nine months, while spending rose to 379.379 billion pesos. Within the spending figure, some 65.061 billion pesos were for debt payments.
Debt costs fell as a percentage of spending to 17.1 percent during the first three quarters from 18.4 percent during the same period the previous year.
